instructions: Keep unchanged: the opening line ('Ila had never been wrong about a distance she had walked herself, so when the tower came up short she walked it again'), the ending laugh ('a bray that had been getting her sent out of dinner tables since she was eleven'), 'Good night, Highness. It's forty', and the north-wall void as written. It pays off in ch32 and ch30 now plants it again.

Lore dump (owner note 6): Ila's speech beginning 'Rohan wrote that the stones at the Shilak Cairn spoke at the thaw...' packs the Bargain, the fourth winter and the archive into one speech. Split it into two parts. Part one covers the stones speaking at the thaw. Then give Kiran one short line, a deflection or a joke that falls flat. Then let his ear-rub carry the weight. Part two covers the fourth winter and the archive. Do not add any new lore.

Book-1 baggage (owner note 6): the opening must stand alone for a new reader. Give the Varun mention a half-clause that says who he is and why he matters in this book's terms. The outline needs the society beat of his going to Taravan in chains, so keep it rather than cut it. Do the same for 'his sister had tied a rope on Ila's brother': add a half-clause such as 'last winter, under the same crossing law', or cut the line. For Kiran having 'stopped looking like a man who expected to be arrested', add a half-clause of reason or cut it. Do not summarise book 1.

Rework the line where Kunal tells her he will speak against her licence so it doesn't lean on 'plainly'. Use 'flat', 'straight out', or just the line itself.
Measurement-for-feeling is Ila's voice. Keep it, but at most once per scene. Allow at most one 'He did not X. He did Y.' construction in the chapter.

Repetitive weighing (owner note 5): the section covering the oath, crime or mercy, and 'Silence was free' says the same point three times. State each element once: the archive oath binds her, the letter accuses his grandfather of walking hers to his death, and silence under the rope costs nothing. Land on 'Silence was free' once. Cut the section by about a third.
Cut the told summary 'It was the most generous thing she had ever watched anyone do.' The beat before it, setting down the mountain 'as a man puts a sleeping child on a bed', already shows it.

Fix the unclear line 'She had held it for an hour at nineteen fingers' depth, in a manner of speaking'. Either cut it, or rewrite it with an explicit referent, for example the Drum ice she sounded in ch15: 'She had stood an hour on nineteen fingers of ice and trusted it more than this.' Drop 'in a manner of speaking'.
Fix the unclear phrase 'one man's grandfather's grave-field'. Rewrite it as something clear that doesn't claim Harish died under the cairn, such as 'the way his grandfather had walked hers'.

Harish's death, fixed sequence (owner note 2). This chapter states it once, clearly. The column of scratched marks ends with Harish's goat and name. The stone shelf holds rotted gloves folded one on another, pair after pair, but it ends with an empty place beside his mark, and his pair is not there. Ila sees the gap and says the sequence aloud to Kunal in one or two sentences: he came here, made his mark, kept his gloves, walked out alive, and folded them on a flat stone on the slope above the third bend, where he died and was found at the thaw. Every payer folded his gloves, and Harish folded his outside. Have Ila notice out loud that he came out alive and died anyway. This plants the hill reading of 'carried' for ch32.
Remove any wording that places Harish's gloves on the shelf or puts his name on a pair of gloves there.

Keep unchanged: Raghu caught by his own rope, with Pasang reading the tallow fingertips. Keep the 'I like you' callback with warm hands and the specific list (pencil leads, 'forty-one', making her laugh when she's furious).

Raghu's purpose, C10 (owner note 3): once Pasang sets the rope down, give him one or two lines that answer both open questions. First, whom Raghu was opening the way for: a winter way over the mountain, found for the regent Pritam and the men waiting on him. Raghu never told Pasang where they would go, which keeps the army question open. Second, where the route-keepers are held: the shepherds' huts in the Hollow Moon bowl, where Dhanu reported Raghu's eight pairs in ch19. Name Hari among them. Kunal's earlier offer ('I'll ask you where they're held') must get this answer on the page.

Pillow talk (owner note 7): cut 'The tower, thirty-nine steps' and 'At Ewe's Rest, for the lambing. The north wall needs checking.' Kunal does not sleep in Pritam's tower, and Garh Neshar's north wall is not at Ewe's Rest. Replace them with a clean plant. Kunal jokes that she can come and check his crooked north wall in spring, recalling ch1's drunk mason. Ila answers 'I'd want a new pace.' Keep it to two or three lines.
Tallow tic (owner note 8): 'the colour of tallow' appears twice here. Keep it once, in Pasang's reading of Raghu's fingertips, and rephrase or cut the other.

Leave the explicit scene's care for her bandaged feet and its adult consent as written.

Keep unchanged: the gloves folded on the table, 'My hands are warm. That tells you nothing,' 'I'd rather break the oath I swore than the one I chose,' the commission as her cost, 'One and three-quarter spans', the double scale bar (spans for the crown, ropes for the hills), and Widow's Knuckle replacing Nimmi's Knuckle. Gauri slip (owner note 1): check every reference, including Gauri's word about the Widow's Ladder and the Dhanu's Rest naming. Gauri is Dhanu's sister. Fix any 'wife' or 'widow' wording.

Harish consistency (owner note 2): in the post room, have Ila tell Rohan the sequence in the same words as ch29. He went in, made his mark, walked out alive, folded his gloves on a flat stone on the slope above the third bend, and died there, found at the thaw. Keep Meera writing 'went in... and came out' and Harish as a person carried. Have Ila or Rohan note in one line that he came out alive and died anyway, which carries the hill reading into ch32.

Hostage keepers follow-through (from owner note 3): add one clause, during the council or the handover, that a licensed pair has gone to the Hollow Moon huts for the held route-keepers. This keeps ch30's payoff from dangling.

Cliffhanger defused offstage (owner note 4): the queen asks Ila, alone, for the rubbing. Make clear which promise to Kunal is at stake. It is her ch30 promise to give Neshar the same as she gives the queen, and the rubbing is what she found under Neshar's way. Kiran's ch3 request to be told where the Bargain is paid can stay as a secondary pull, but it must not carry the dilemma alone. End the chapter on her refusal, spoken live to the queen in the room: 'Not alone.' Add the queen's one-line reaction and a final line on what it costs Ila. Replace the current closing line 'Whichever way she moved, she would be breaking faith with one of them' with this live exchange.

Word tics (owner note 8): keep at most one 'plain', 'plainly' or 'the plain thing'. This chapter stacks 'He did not X. He did Y.', so keep at most one. Keep spans-for-feelings to once per scene. The pace re-measurement is literal measurement and stays.

Cliffhanger defused offstage (owner note 4): cut the past-perfect recap ('Not alone,' Ila had told the queen, and anything like it). Ch31 now plays that exchange live. Open in scene at dusk at the cairn. The queen brings out the rubbing in front of Kunal, and Kiran is present, as the consequence of Ila's refusal. If a link is needed, use one present-action beat, not a summary.

Harish consistency (owner note 2): change 'carried down at the thaw' to 'found on the slope at the thaw and carried down', or similar, so it matches ch29 and ch31. In the two readings of 'carried till no thaw', have Ila use the fact that Harish walked out alive as her evidence for the hill sense of 'carried across'. The queen holds that the mountain took its life anyway. No one can prove either.

North-wall plant payoff (owner note 7): when the rider reports Pritam's escape by the stair inside the north wall, give one beat, a look or half a line between Ila and Kunal, recalling his ch30 joke about his crooked north wall. Do not explain it.

Raghu thread (owner note 3, optional support): the rider may add in half a line that Raghu's loyalists' bells were found on the east tracks with Pritam's. This ties the hunt to the escape without answering whose army it is.
